interface.signature: def findString(N: int, K: int) -> str:

preconditions.description: The total number of possible strings of length N is strictly between 1 and 4096.

postconditions.expression: all(c in '0123456789' for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: The returned string consists only of digit characters.

postconditions.expression: all(int(c) < K for c in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every character in the returned string represents a digit strictly less than K.
The length of the returned string is exactly K^N + N - 1, which is the theoretical minimum length for a De Bruijn sequence of order N on K symbols.

postconditions.expression: all(any(return_value[i:i+N] == ''.join(str((j // (K**(N-1-x))) % K) for x in range(N)) for i in range(len(return_value) - N + 1)) for j in range(K**N))
postconditions.description: Every possible string of length N formed by digits 0 to K-1 appears as a substring in the returned string.
